lessons.name: THE CONTROL: THE BOUND CAN FAIL. With 16-bit handles the store's 71,621 leaves would outnumber the 65,536 handles available, so two leaves would be forced to share one — pigeonhole, not chance — and the store refuses any collision. The odds above are a property of the widths chosen, and a width too small is refuted by the same arithmetic; that is why a handle carries 32 bits.

lessons.name: A GUESSED ADDRESS DOES NOT LAND. The ledger holds 71,017 distinct addresses, every one a v8 uuid with 122 free bits, so a forger who invents an address and frames it as sealed hits a real one with odds below 2^-105: 71,017 × 2^105 < 2^122. forensics() flags every miss as a false address — run here on a forged address (flagged) and a sealed one (passed) — so a false trial cannot survive except by that chance, and the chance is sealed. Counted from the ledger at generation, never typed.

lessons.name: A GUESSED HANDLE RARELY LANDS EITHER. The handle store holds 71,621 leaves in a 32-bit handle space, so a guessed handle names an occupied leaf with odds below 2^-15: 71,621 × 2^15 < 2^32. The odds are far weaker than an address's, which is why a handle is only ever the PATH to a leaf and the leaf itself carries the full uuid that forensics() checks.
